text:
amar: quick sync - we need to finalize how RBAC + scope caching interacts. ran into a bug in staging where role changes didn't apply because scope cache keys missed role updates.

sophie: repro?

amar: sequence: key scoped to project:alpha assigned role=reader. later we added writer role. clients still had cached authz results and couldn't write. cache key was only binder_key_id + resource, missing role-set hash.

lee: easy fix: include role version or hash in cache key. but that requires bumping on every role change. how do we propagate role-set version?
tom: policy service should emit a versioned change event for role bindings. routers subscribe and invalidate matching cache entries.

amar: additional nuance: some tokens are ephemeral and short (15s) -> caching not needed. for longer ephemerals (5m) we do. need clear TTL heuristics.
sophie: suggested heuristic: ephemeral_ttl <= 60s -> no caching. ephemeral_ttl > 60s -> cache but include role-version.

policy-bot: guidance: see policy 'authz-cache-v1' https://redwood.internal/policies/authz-cache-v1

lee: edgecase: when a role is removed and re-added rapidly (flapping) we may get cache churn. maybe a soft-ttl with grace period: on role removal, mark cache entries stale but let them expire after 30s to avoid auth storms.
amar: I'm uneasy about letting stale entries linger after role removal, that's an authorization hole. instead: if role removal is observed, force immediate invalidation. to prevent storms, use a jittered backoff for policy propagation and rate-limit rechecks.

tom: also consider batch invalidation: when many role changes happen, send a single delta event with affected principals. routers apply in one pass.
sophie: UX: Console should show affected tokens and a 'force-invalidate' button. and in incident page show 'invalidate-cached-ephemerals' quick action.

amar: decision items:
1) include role-set-hash in authz cache key
2) ephemeral caching heuristic (>60s allowed)
3) immediate invalidation on role removal, but with propagation backoff to avoid DDOS on policy service
4) Console force-invalidate action and incident quick action

lee: votes: +1 all. sophie: +1. tom: +1.
amar: I'll update the authz-cache mini-RFC and add tests for role-change propagation.

amar: thanks :thumbsup:
